trial_court: Court of Learned District Judge, Family Court, Bhiwani

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: wife, seeking transfer of petition filed by husband

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife seeks transfer of petition filed by respondent-husband under Section 13(1) (ia)(ib) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Petitioner-wife has two minor daughters and is financially dependent on her parents.

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, and their behavioural pattern.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants while deciding transfer applications.
legal_principles.held: Further, Hon'ble the Apex Court in Rajani Kishor Pradeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237, has observed that 'while deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one court to another should ordinary be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.'
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pradeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should ensure that leniency given to female litigants is not misused.
legal_principles.held: However, to avoid any misuse of the lenient view by the female litigants, Hon'ble the Apex Court in Anindita Das v. Srijit Das, (2006) 9 SCC 197, has also cautioned that the Courts should ensure that such leniency given to the female litigants should not be misused.
cited_cases: Anindita Das v. Srijit Das, (2006) 9 SCC 197

outcome.final_order: Petition transferred to any Court of competent jurisdiction at Gurugram.
